title: Abraham will pray for Abimelech and he will live
summary: God warned Abimelech in a dream that he was a dead man for taking Sarah, but said Abraham was a prophet who would pray for him and he would live. Abraham prayed, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants.

title: Aaron is already on his way to meet Moses
summary: At the burning bush God told Moses that Aaron was already coming out to meet him and would speak for him. Aaron met Moses at the mount of God, and he spoke to the elders in Moses' place.

title: Aaron's rod will become a serpent before Pharaoh
summary: God said that when Pharaoh asked for a miracle, Aaron's rod would become a serpent when he threw it down. It did, and it swallowed the rods of Pharaoh's magicians.

title: The dust of Egypt will become lice
summary: God said that when Aaron struck the dust, it would become lice throughout Egypt. It did, and the magicians could not copy it and said, "This is the finger of God."

title: Furnace ashes will become boils on man and beast
summary: God said that ashes from the furnace thrown toward heaven would become fine dust and break out as boils on people and animals across Egypt. It happened, and even the magicians were struck and could not stand before Moses.

title: Darkness over Egypt, with light in Israel's dwellings
summary: God said darkness that could be felt would cover Egypt when Moses stretched out his hand. Egypt lay in thick darkness for three days, but all the children of Israel had light where they lived.

title: Pharaoh's servants will bow and beg Israel to leave
summary: Moses told Pharaoh that after the last plague his servants would come down, bow before him and say, "Get thee out." That night Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and the Egyptians pressed Israel to leave in haste.

title: Israel will cross the sea on dry ground
summary: God told Moses to lift up his rod over the sea, divide it, and Israel would go through on dry ground. An east wind parted the waters all night and Israel walked through the sea on dry land, with the water a wall on either side.

title: Double manna on the sixth day and none on the Sabbath
prophet: God to Moses; Moses to Israel
summary: God said the people would gather twice as much manna on the sixth day, and Moses said none would be found on the seventh. On the sixth day they gathered a double portion, and those who went out on the Sabbath found nothing.

title: On the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai
summary: God told Moses to get the people ready, because on the third day He would come down on Mount Sinai in a thick cloud where everyone could see. On the third day there was thunder, lightning, a thick cloud and a trumpet blast, and the LORD came down on the mountain in fire.

title: God will send hornets ahead of Israel to drive out the nations
summary: At Sinai God promised to send the hornet ahead of Israel to drive out the Hivite, Canaanite and Hittite. At the end of the conquest Joshua reminded Israel that God had sent the hornet before them, which drove out the two kings of the Amorites, "not with thy sword, nor with thy bow".

title: The glory of the LORD will appear at the priests' ordination
summary: Moses told the congregation to offer the first sacrifices because "today the LORD will appear unto you". When Aaron finished, the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people and fire came out from before the LORD and burned up the offering on the altar.

title: God will put Moses' spirit on seventy elders
summary: God told Moses to gather seventy elders, and He would take of the spirit on Moses and put it on them so they could share his burden. When they gathered, the Spirit rested on them and they prophesied, including Eldad and Medad in the camp.

title: If you go up now you will fall before your enemies
summary: After the 40-year sentence the people decided to invade anyway. Moses warned that the LORD was not with them and they would fall by the sword. They went up, and the Amalekites and Canaanites struck them and chased them back to Hormah.

title: The rock at Kadesh will give water (Meribah)
summary: In the 40th year at Kadesh, God told Moses to speak to the rock in front of the people and it would give out water for them and their animals. Moses struck the rock twice and water came out in abundance. (This is a different event from the rock at Horeb in Exodus 17.)

title: Sihon king of Heshbon will be given into Israel's hand
summary: God told Moses He had begun to hand Sihon the Amorite and his land over to Israel. Sihon came out to fight at Jahaz and Israel struck him and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, including Heshbon.

title: Fear not Og king of Bashan; he is given into your hand
summary: As Og the giant king of Bashan marched out to Edrei, God told Moses not to fear, because Og, his people and his land had been given into his hand. Israel struck Og until none of his people were left and took sixty walled cities of Argob.

title: Phinehas' line will hold an everlasting priesthood

fulfilled.label: c. 1001 BC (Zadok made high priest under Solomon)

summary: God gave Phinehas, son of Eleazar, a covenant of an everlasting priesthood for his zeal. The office passed for a time to Eli of Ithamar's line, but when Solomon removed Abiathar he made Zadok, a descendant of Phinehas, high priest. Zadok's line held the office into the Second Temple period, and Ezekiel names the sons of Zadok as the priests of the future temple.

title: Moses will die after avenging Israel on Midian
summary: God told Moses to avenge Israel on the Midianites and "afterward shalt thou be gathered unto thy people". Israel defeated Midian and killed its five kings and Balaam, and soon afterward Moses died on Mount Nebo, before the crossing of the Jordan.

title: God will choose one place to put His name (Jerusalem)
summary: Moses told Israel that once they were in the land, they must bring their offerings to the one place the LORD would choose to put His name. Centuries later God told Solomon, at the dedication of the Temple, "I have chosen this place to myself for an house of sacrifice," and He named Jerusalem as the city He had chosen.

title: Benjamin: the LORD will dwell between his shoulders
summary: In his blessing Moses said the LORD would dwell "between his shoulders" (Benjamin's). Jebus (Jerusalem) fell to Benjamin's lot on the border with Judah, and the Temple, where God's glory filled the house, was built on Mount Moriah within that border.

title: This day God will begin to magnify Joshua as He did Moses
summary: Before the Jordan crossing God told Joshua He would begin that day to make him great in Israel's eyes, so they would know He was with him as He had been with Moses. After the crossing, "the LORD magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they feared him, as they feared Moses."

title: The lot will expose the man who took the devoted things
summary: After the defeat at Ai, God said He would point out the guilty tribe, family, household and man, one by one. The lot fell on Judah, then the Zarhites, then Zabdi, then Achan, who confessed that he had hidden a garment, silver and gold from Jericho in his tent.

title: Ehud: the LORD has given Moab into your hand
summary: After killing Eglon, Ehud called Israel out, saying the LORD had given their Moabite enemies into their hand. They held the fords of the Jordan, killed about ten thousand Moabites, and the land had rest for eighty years. (Year counted back from Deborah, c. 1209 BC: 20 years under Jabin, 80 years of rest.)

title: Samuel: return to the LORD and He will deliver you from the Philistines
summary: Samuel told Israel to put away their foreign gods, and the LORD would deliver them from the Philistines. At Mizpah the LORD thundered against the Philistines, Israel routed them, Samuel set up the stone Ebenezer, and the Philistines did not come into Israel's borders again in Samuel's days.

title: Samuel: the king will take your sons, daughters, fields and a tenth
summary: When Israel asked for a king, Samuel warned that he would take their sons for chariots and labour, their daughters for his kitchens, the best of their fields, and a tenth of their produce, and that they would cry out because of him. Under Solomon there were horsemen and chariots, district taxes, and forced labour gangs for the Temple, and at his death the people begged Rehoboam to lighten "the grievous service of thy father".

title: Go down to Keilah: the Philistines will be given into your hand
summary: When the Philistines raided Keilah, the LORD told David twice to go, because He would give the Philistines into his hand. David's men struck the Philistines, took their cattle and saved Keilah. (The later oracle that Keilah would hand him over to Saul is already in the database.)

title: David's wives will be taken openly by one of his own
summary: Nathan said God would raise up evil from David's own house and give his wives to his neighbour "in the sight of this sun", in public, though David had sinned in secret. During his revolt Absalom pitched a tent on the palace roof and went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

title: A son named Solomon will have rest and peace all his reign
summary: God told David he would have a son who would be "a man of rest", named Solomon (from shalom), and He would give Israel peace and quiet in his days. Solomon reigned without war, with "peace on all sides round about him", and Judah and Israel lived safely, "every man under his vine and under his fig tree".

title: Ravens will feed Elijah at the brook Cherith
summary: At the start of the drought God sent Elijah to the brook Cherith and said He had commanded the ravens to feed him there. Ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank from the brook until it dried up.

title: God will send rain at the end of the drought
prophet: God to Elijah; Elijah to Ahab
summary: In the third year God told Elijah to show himself to Ahab, "and I will send rain upon the earth". After Carmel, Elijah told Ahab he could hear the sound of abundant rain. A cloud the size of a man's hand rose from the sea, and a heavy rain followed.

title: Elisha: the waters of Jericho are healed for good
summary: The men of Jericho told Elisha the water was bad and the land barren. He threw salt into the spring and declared, in the LORD's name, that it was healed and would no longer cause death or barrenness. The writer of Kings says the waters stayed healed "unto this day".

title: Azariah son of Oded: seek the LORD and your work will be rewarded
summary: After the victory over Zerah, Azariah told Asa that the LORD would be with Judah while they were with Him, and that their work would be rewarded. Asa removed the idols and renewed the covenant, and "the LORD gave them rest round about", with no more war until Asa's 35th year. (Year from Rehoboam's 5th year = 957 BC.)

title: Neco's warning, "from the mouth of God": Josiah will be destroyed if he fights
prophet: Pharaoh Neco (words "from the mouth of God", 35:22)
summary: As Neco marched to Carchemish, he warned Josiah not to oppose God, who was with him, "that he destroy thee not". The Chronicler says these were words from the mouth of God. Josiah fought anyway at Megiddo, was hit by archers, and died. (Secular date 609 BC.)

title: Philistia, rejoice not: a worse serpent will come out of the root

fulfilled.label: c. 720 BC (Sargon II at Raphia; Ashdod 711 BC)

fulfilment: 2 Kings 18:8; Assyrian annals of Sargon II
summary: In the year Ahaz died, Isaiah warned the Philistines not to celebrate the breaking of the rod that struck them, because a cockatrice and a fiery flying serpent would come out of the serpent's root, and smoke would come from the north. Hezekiah struck the Philistines as far as Gaza, and Sargon II defeated Hanunu of Gaza at Raphia (720 BC) and later took Ashdod (711 BC).

title: Eliakim will be given Shebna's office over the palace
summary: Isaiah said God would call His servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah, clothe him with Shebna's robe and give him the key of the house of David. When Sennacherib's officials came to Jerusalem, Eliakim son of Hilkiah was "over the household" and Shebna had become the scribe. (Johnson's #74, Shebna's fall, is already in the database; this is the separate promise to Eliakim. Secular date 701 BC.)

title: Egypt's help against Assyria will be in vain
summary: Isaiah warned Judah's leaders that the alliance with Egypt would bring shame, not help, because "the Egyptians shall help in vain". Sennacherib's envoys called Egypt a "broken reed", and Sennacherib's annals record that he defeated the Egyptian and Cushite relief army at Eltekeh. Jerusalem was saved by the LORD, not by Egypt.

sources.name: Encyclopedia of the Bible: Elteke, Eltekeh (Bible Gateway)

title: Micah: the enemy will reach Jerusalem's gate through Lachish and the lowland
summary: Micah lamented that Samaria's wound had reached Judah, "even to the gate of Jerusalem", and named the lowland towns (Lachish, Moresheth-gath, Mareshah, Achzib) that would fall. Sennacherib took the fortified cities of Judah, besieged Lachish and sent his army from there to the gate of Jerusalem. The siege of Lachish is shown on his palace reliefs at Nineveh.

title: Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, then trade again

fulfilled.label: c. 535 BC (Tyrians trade cedar for the Second Temple)

summary: Isaiah said Tyre would be forgotten for seventy years, "according to the days of one king", and afterward would return to her trade with the kingdoms of the earth, and her profits would go to those who serve the LORD. Tyre was among the nations that served Babylon its seventy years. Under Persia it traded again, and Tyrians and Sidonians supplied cedar for the Second Temple in exchange for food and oil.

title: Of the Temple: "Thy foundation shall be laid" (by Cyrus' decree)
summary: Isaiah named Cyrus as God's shepherd, who would say to Jerusalem, "Thou shalt be built", and to the Temple, "Thy foundation shall be laid." Cyrus' decree ordered the house of God rebuilt, and in the second year after the return the builders laid the foundation of the Temple with trumpets and singing. (Cyrus freeing the exiles is already in the database as #92.)

title: Bel bows down, Nebo stoops: Babylon's idols carried off
summary: Isaiah pictured Babylon's gods Bel (Marduk) and Nebo bowing down, loaded on animals and carried into captivity, and Jeremiah said Bel would be put to shame and Merodach broken in pieces. After Babylon revolted, Xerxes took the great statue of Bel from the Esagila temple and killed the priest who tried to stop him (Herodotus). Arrian says Xerxes also tore the temple down.

title: The broad walls of Babylon will be broken down
summary: In the oracle sent to Babylon in Zedekiah's 4th year, Jeremiah said "the broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly broken, and her high gates shall be burned with fire", and that "the wall of Babylon shall fall". Cyrus took the city without a fight, but after Babylon revolted, Darius I took it again after a long siege and pulled down its walls and carried off its gates (Herodotus).

title: Ezekiel's wife will be taken suddenly as a sign
summary: On the day the siege began, God told Ezekiel He would take away "the desire of thine eyes" with a stroke, and that he must not mourn. Ezekiel spoke to the people in the morning, his wife died that evening, and he did as he was told, as a sign that Jerusalem's Temple, the desire of their eyes, would be profaned.

title: Vengeance on Edom by the hand of God's people Israel
summary: Ezekiel said God would take vengeance on Edom for what it did to Judah, and that He would do it "by the hand of my people Israel". Judas Maccabeus struck the Idumeans, and John Hyrcanus conquered Idumea, took Adora and Marisa, and made the Idumeans be circumcised and live as Jews. Edom ceased to be a separate people. (Obadiah's "no survivor", with AD 70, is already in the database.)

sources.name: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews (Project Gutenberg)

title: Sidon: pestilence and blood in her streets

fulfilled.label: c. 345 BC (Artaxerxes III; dates given 351–344 BC)

summary: Ezekiel said God would send pestilence into Sidon and blood into her streets, with the wounded falling by the sword on every side. Unlike Tyre, Sidon was not promised to be wiped out for good. When Sidon revolted against Persia, its king Tennes betrayed it to Artaxerxes III. The Sidonians burned their ships and then the city with themselves inside, and more than 40,000 died (Diodorus). Sidon was later rebuilt.

title: Egypt will be the lowliest kingdom, never again ruling the nations
fulfilment: Herodotus 3.1-16; history of Persian, Greek and Roman Egypt
summary: Ezekiel said Egypt would come back as a lowly kingdom, "the basest of the kingdoms", and would never again exalt itself above the nations or rule over them. After Persia conquered it, Egypt was ruled by Persians, then Macedonian Ptolemies, then Rome. Its own power never again reached into Asia as it had under the great pharaohs.

title: There will be no more a native prince of the land of Egypt

fulfilled.label: 343 BC (Nectanebo II, the last native pharaoh, flees)

summary: Ezekiel said God would destroy the idols of Noph (Memphis) and "there shall be no more a prince of the land of Egypt". Native kings came back for a while after Persian rule, but when Artaxerxes III reconquered Egypt, Nectanebo II fled south. He was the last native Egyptian to rule Egypt as pharaoh: after him came Persians, Macedonians, Ptolemies, Romans and others.

title: The writing on the wall: Belshazzar's kingdom given to the Medes and Persians

given.label: 537 BC (Johnson; secular 539 BC), the night of the feast

fulfilled.label: 537 BC (Johnson; secular 12 Oct 539 BC), that night

summary: Daniel read the words on the wall: God had numbered and finished Belshazzar's kingdom, he was weighed and found wanting, and the kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians. "In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain", and Darius the Mede took the kingdom. (The older prophecies of Babylon's fall are already in the database; this is Daniel's own prediction that night.)

title: The tax-raiser will be destroyed within a few days, not in anger or battle
summary: The vision foretold a king who would send a "raiser of taxes" through the glory of the kingdom and would then be destroyed within a few days, "neither in anger, nor in battle". Seleucus IV sent Heliodorus to seize the Temple treasury and was soon murdered by Heliodorus in a palace plot, not in war. (His order against the Temple is already in the database as #117.)

title: He will scatter plunder and riches more than his fathers did
summary: The vile king of the north would enter peaceably into the richest places of the province and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers' fathers had done, scattering plunder, spoil and riches among his followers. 1 Maccabees says Antiochus IV gave gifts "more lavishly than preceding kings", and Polybius describes him throwing money to people in the streets.

title: Throw me into the sea and it will be calm
summary: In the storm, Jonah told the sailors to throw him overboard and the sea would be calm, because the storm was on his account. When they threw him into the sea, "the sea ceased from her raging", and the sailors feared the LORD and offered a sacrifice.
